attempts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset: TRUE HAND-DRAWN IN-BETWEEN animation sprites for Mosey Gemini.
Input1 is the existing sixteen KEYFRAMES, four columns by four rows. Input2 is the original character identity reference. This task outputs ONLY sixteen NEW MIDPOINT drawings that will be inserted BETWEEN the original keyframes. DO NOT output the keyframes again. DO NOT blend, ghost, fade, duplicate contours, stretch/warp a whole image or merely change opacity. Draw anatomically coherent genuinely intermediate elbow/hand/head/eye/mouth positions, with one solid outlined character per cell.
Output ONE FOUR-column FOUR-row square PNG sheet, matching Input1's exact cell layout, framing and pixel drawing scale as closely as possible. Input1 is1254x1254. Every pose occupies the same cell center and ground line as the corresponding row of Input1. Preserve the exact SAME head width and short-limbed squat proportions; sitting only lowers joints, never rescales the whole figure. Transparent background with full true alpha. Keep complete hair/ears/tail/hands within the cell; wide clear transparent gutters. NO background, ground shadow, labels, grid lines, letters, props, effects or external hands.
Strict identity: blue-purple long hair broad locks, dark thick outline, simple cel shading, big head and tiny body, blue cat ears pink centers, small curl, VIEWER-RIGHT star hair clip, VIEWER-LEFT magenta eye, VIEWER-RIGHT amber eye, navy-purple/white dress and chest star, boots, ONE attached fluffy blue-purple tail on VIEWER-RIGHT. Never swap eyes or sides. No new rendering style or extra detail.
Grid mapping, zero-based: output row R col0 = midpoint between old row R col0 and col1; output col1 = midpoint between old col1 and col2; output col2 = midpoint between old col2 and col3; output col3 = midpoint on return from old col3 to old col0 (except the explicitly stated sitting-down exception).
You are an animator creating missing drawings, NOT a contact-sheet copier. Follow the actual neighboring key poses in Input1. Smooth half-lidded transitions, half-raised hands and partial head rotation must be visibly between the endpoint positions. Body grounding, hair volume and attached accessories stay stable.
ROW1 LOOKING: col0 head/gaze halfway toward the old left-look pose; col1 head/gaze moving through the middle between old left and right look; col2 halfway returning toward old neutral; col3 subtly transitioning neutral gaze back toward the old first-frame gaze. Keep head rotation restrained and feet planted.
ROW2 SITTING-DOWN: col0 knees slightly bending, hands midway from sides toward knees, pelvis between old standing and bend; col1 half-squat between old bend and deep squat, head lowered correspondingly but identical size; col2 pelvis halfway between old squat and seated, knees folding and hands easing down. IMPORTANT col3 is midpoint from old ROW2 COL3 fully seated to old ROW3 COL0 awake seated loop start: remain FULLY SEATED, open eyes, no rise to standing, no change of head scale.
ROW3 AWAKE SEATED: col0 tiny eye/shoulder transition between old seated front gaze and slight side gaze; col1 hand halfway from knee to cheek (elbow bends), head halfway toward hand; col2 hand halfway lowering from cheek to knee with head returning; col3 subtle open-eye transition from old last seated pose to old first seated pose. NEVER sleep or close both eyes here.
ROW4 YAWN: col0 hand halfway from chest to mouth, mouth beginning to open and eyelids three-quarter closed; col1 yawn releasing, hand halfway down to chest, mouth partly closed and eyelids slightly reopening; col2 hand halfway from chest to side and eyes opening; col3 hand halfway rising from side toward chest for the next yawn preparation. Do NOT reproduce fully closed-eye yawn keyframe; these are transitional drawings.
Output sixteen clear, solid NEW middle poses.

Use case: identity-preserve. Create precise new hand-drawn animation IN-BETWEENS.
Input1 is a paired-endpoint storyboard: FOUR PAIR-SLOTS across and FOUR ROWS down. There are32 figures total: within each slot, the LEFT figure is endpoint A and the RIGHT figure is endpoint B. Input2 is the unchanged identity reference.
Your OUTPUT must be a SQUARE FOUR-by-FOUR sheet of ONLY SIXTEEN figures, ONE newly drawn halfway pose per input pair-slot. Do NOT copy the32-figure input layout. Each output slot corresponds to the same input pair-slot. Synthesize the halfway pose from the TWO endpoints in that slot. Do NOT choose or reproduce either endpoint. Preserve style, scale, head size, foot contact, and camera.
This is physical keyframe inbetweening: place wrists, elbows, head rotation, knees, pelvis and eyelids at approximately50% of the distance between A and B. Draw one clean solid silhouette without blending or double contours. Halfway mouth shape, half-lidded eyes, hand/elbow midway, knees half-bent. If A and B are essentially the same neutral pose, retain that neutral pose without inventing a new movement. The purpose is to remove the visible jump when playing A -> NEW -> B.
Particularly inspect each pair's wrist position: the new wrist must not remain at either A or B. In a knee-to-cheek movement the new hand is at CHEST height, not still at the cheek. In a clap approach the hands are close with aboutHALF the original gap, not still widely separated and not touching. In a clip adjustment the hand is halfway between shoulder and temple. When lowering chest-height hand to side, the new hand is at WAIST height. For sitting, pelvis height should be exactly halfway between the two supplied postures while head size remains constant.
Output2048x2048,4columns4rows, complete full characters with transparent margins. True transparent alpha background. No text/numbers/grid/shadow/effects. Match input rendering: big round head, tiny body, thick dark outlines, blue-purple hair, VIEWER-LEFT magenta eye, VIEWER-RIGHT amber eye, VIEWER-RIGHT star clip, white-purple/navy dress with chest star, cat ears, attached blue-purple tail on VIEWER-RIGHT. Do not change costume, head proportions, side placement or identity. Feet anchored consistently. No extra anatomy or props.
The input pair-slots ALREADY encode the return transitions; treat each slot independently. The original keyframe mapping behind these pairs is:

ROW1 LOOKING: col0 head/gaze halfway toward the old left-look pose; col1 head/gaze moving through the middle between old left and right look; col2 halfway returning toward old neutral; col3 subtly transitioning neutral gaze back toward the old first-frame gaze. Keep head rotation restrained and feet planted.
ROW2 SITTING-DOWN: col0 knees slightly bending, hands midway from sides toward knees, pelvis between old standing and bend; col1 half-squat between old bend and deep squat, head lowered correspondingly but identical size; col2 pelvis halfway between old squat and seated, knees folding and hands easing down. IMPORTANT col3 is midpoint from old ROW2 COL3 fully seated to old ROW3 COL0 awake seated loop start: remain FULLY SEATED, open eyes, no rise to standing, no change of head scale.
ROW3 AWAKE SEATED: col0 tiny eye/shoulder transition between old seated front gaze and slight side gaze; col1 hand halfway from knee to cheek (elbow bends), head halfway toward hand; col2 hand halfway lowering from cheek to knee with head returning; col3 subtle open-eye transition from old last seated pose to old first seated pose. NEVER sleep or close both eyes here.
ROW4 YAWN: col0 hand halfway from chest to mouth, mouth beginning to open and eyelids three-quarter closed; col1 yawn releasing, hand halfway down to chest, mouth partly closed and eyelids slightly reopening; col2 hand halfway from chest to side and eyes opening; col3 hand halfway rising from side toward chest for the next yawn preparation. Do NOT reproduce fully closed-eye yawn keyframe; these are transitional drawings.
Output sixteen clear, solid NEW middle poses.
